citation: [William Howard Taft, full length, standing, facing slightly right, with Elihu Root], photographic print, copyright 1904 (the print is stamped 'Copyrighted 1904 Clinedinst, Wash. D.C.'). Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, LC-USZ62-48890 (item 2006685745).
author: Clinedinst, Washington, D.C. (the studio stamp on the print)
repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division. Master TIFF 3a48890u.tif (1077 x 1536, greyscale), read at tile.loc.gov.
locator: The whole print: Taft standing full length on the left, Root standing behind a desk on the right, both at about three metres.
rights_note: LOC rights advisory: 'No known restrictions on publication.' Published 1904. Used only as a reference picture the 1904 gentleman is judged against and as the cut of his day dress (T-3441); nothing is traced or sampled from it.
access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-07 (T-3441) from the master TIFF. Taft (then Secretary of War, 46) in a dark single-breasted frock coat whose skirts reach just below the knee, buttoned at the waist, with pale striped trousers, a turned-down collar and a dark bow tie, low black shoes. Root (59; slim, moustache, spectacles) in a dark frock coat open over a dark high-cut waistcoat, a tall wing collar and a dark tie, his trousers dark. A studio portrait in Washington, not of Chicago.
note: One of the 1904 gentleman reference set's photographs (data/people_match/reference_sets/gentleman_1904.json). Root is the nearest picture found of a slim, spectacled, moustached man of Glessner's age in day dress in 1904; no likeness of Glessner is drawn from it.
what_it_supplies: the frock coat of 1904: dark, single-breasted, lapels rolled to the chest, skirts to the knee
a high-cut dark waistcoat, a tall standing or wing collar and a dark tie on a man of about sixty
trousers worn straight to the shoe, with a small break
what_it_does_not_supply: anything about Chicago, the Glessner household or John J. Glessner; no likeness is asserted
